newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to test-fire two more U.S. Hawk missiles.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to test-fire two more U.S. Hawk missiles.

text.p: Taiwan will test-fire two U.S. Hawk missiles in the Taiwan Strait on April 1, continuing a drill seen as bolstering the island's defences against China, military officials said on Thursday.
They brushed off speculation that the test had anything to do with reports that China was planning large-scale manoeuvres in three nearby provinces to intimidate Taiwan.

"The test is just a two-part practice of the army's Fairy Arrow Operation No. 37," a defence official told Reuters. "Our last round, which was announced through newspaper advertisements, was held on March 19."
He said the test was long-scheduled, routine practice.
Other defence officials said the missile test had nothing to do with recent news reports that China was preparing to stage large-scale joint-forces manoeuvres in three coastal provinces.
Taipei's United Daily News said on March 23 the drills would be staged in April in Fujian, Guangdong and Zhejiang provinces.
Taiwan's defence ministry has said it had detected no signs that China would hold military drills.

The army on March 19 test-fired two medium-range U.S. Hawk missiles into the open sea from a northern base at Tanshui, resuming an annual test that had been suspended a year earlier at a time of acute tensions with China.
Commercial planes and vessels were asked not to go near the designated splash zone. Defence officials said the same would apply to the April 1 test.
The military suspended the missile tests and other large scale drills in March 1996 to avoid exacerbating tensions with China, the island's rival since a civil war split them in 1949.
The suspension followed eight months of war games mounted by Beijing in waters near Taiwan that reached a peak in the weeks before island's historic March 23 presidential election.
China views Taiwan as a rebel-held province that must be brought under mainland control, by force if necessary.
